For Respondent(s) :
Mr. Bhawani Shankar Sharma, PP HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR UPMAN Order 15/07/2024 Heard learned counsel for the applicants-appellants and learned Public Prosecutor on the applications for suspension of sentences.

The applicants-appellants herein have been convicted for offences under Sections 363, 366-A &
376-D of IPC and Section [2024:RJ-JP:29523] (2 of 5) [SOSA-975/2022] 5/6 of POCSO Act vide judgment dated 14.07.2022 passed by learned Special Judge, POCSO Cases, No.1, Alwar, District Alwar in Sessions Case No.79/2018 (154/2016) and have been sentenced to maximum punishment of 20 years.
Learned counsel for the applicants submit that learned trial court has erred in convicting and sentencing the applicants as mentioned above.
Learned trial court has not appreciated the evidence in right and correct perspective.

Counsel appearing on behalf of applicant Roop Singh submits that there is no allegation against the applicant in the statements of prosecutrix recorded under Sections Shriram @ Mukesh S/O Ramkaran vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jp:29523) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27789250/
1 161 & 164 Cr.P.C of commission of rape.

entities.text: O Ramkaran vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jp:29523)
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
It is submitted that later on, during the course of trial,
prosecutrix changed her version and levelled allegation of rape against the applicant.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of applicant Shriram @ Mukesh submits that prosecutrix was in love with the applicant Shriram and she left her parental home on her own free will and volition.
Prosecutrix travelled with the applicant from her home to Jaipur.
From Jaipur, they went to Delhi and then to Chandigarh.
It is submitted that during this period, no complaint was made by prosecutrix.
Learned counsel appearing for both the applicants submit that during the course of trial, applicants were on bail and there is no allegation against them of misusing the liberty of bail.
It is submitted that there is no medical corroboration of the allegation levelled by the prosecutrix.

They submit that PW-13 Dr. Jitendra Pal Singh, who conducted medical examination of the prosecutrix, in his statement clearly stated that the organs of the prosecutrix [2024:RJ-JP:29523] (3 of 5)
[SOSA-975/2022] were fully developed as per her age and no sign of sexual assault was found on her body.
FSL report does not corroborate the allegation of prosecutrix as no semen was found in the samples.

It is further submitted that applicant Roop Singh has served incarceration for a period of 2 years and 7 months including remission while applicant Shriram @ Mukesh has served incarceration for a period of 2 years and 10 months including remission.
There are bleak chances of this appeal being heard and decided in near future.
Learned State counsel admits that there is bleak chance of hearing of the appeal in near future as large number of appeals are pending before this Court.
He, however, opposes the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicants.
He submits that there is specific allegation against applicant Shriram of commission of rape with the prosecutrix and applicant Roop Singh was with him.
It is submitted that age of prosecutrix was found nearly 16 years at the time of incident.

Upon a consideration of the arguments advanced on behalf of the applicants and having regard to the facts and circumstances as available on the record especially looking to the period of sentence already served by the applicants and bleak chances of appeal being decided in near future, but without commenting anything on merits and demerits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for suspending the sentences awarded to the accused applicants during pendency of the instant appeals.

Accordingly, these applications for suspension of sentence filed under Section 389 Cr.P.C. are allowed and it is ordered that the sentences passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Cases,
[2024:RJ-JP:29523] (4 of 5) [SOSA-975/2022] No.1, Alwar, District Alwar vide judgment dated 14.07.2022 in Sessions Case No.79/2018 (154/2016) against the appellants- applicants (1) Roop Singh @ Roopchand S/o Pooran Chand (2) Shriram @ Mukesh S/o Ramkaran, shall remain suspended till final disposal of the aforesaid appeal and each of them shall be released on bail,
provided each of them executes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for their appearance in this court on 14.08.2024 and whenever ordered to do so till the disposal of the appeal on the conditions indicated below:-
Shriram
